_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::fpsi#2. The rule holds — MAT_StructPoro's MATID must point at a structural material — but the Signal was fabricated and the two ways of getting it wrong differ. On upstream fpsi_ofsiinterface.4C.yaml (MAT 1 = MAT_StructPoro, MATID 6 -> MAT_ElastHyper): pointing MATID at the MAT_fluid gives 'Mat::StructPoro: underlying material should be of type Mat::So3Material' from mat/4C_mat_structporo.cpp line 109, while pointing it at an undefined ID gives "Material 'MAT 99' could not be found" from mat/4C_mat_par_bundle.cpp line 36 — a different file, so grepping for the structporo file after that typo finds nothing (UNDEFMAT_IN_STRUCTPORO_FILE=0 against FLUIDMAT_IN_STRUCTPORO_FILE=1). The quoted phrase 'StructPoro inner material must be elastic' appears in neither arm. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C (2026.2.0-dev, commit 89519cfe76).
expect_in_output: Mat::StructPoro: underlying material should be of type Mat::So3Material

_mutation.note: remove the wrong-type pathology: point MATID back at the elastic material. FLUID_ARM_MATID:6 is a forbidden token and the So3Material abort vanishes, so the fixture must go red.
remove the undefined-ID pathology: point MATID back at a defined material. UNDEF_ARM_MATID:6 is a forbidden token and the 'could not be found' abort vanishes, so the fixture must go red.
